newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank lifts Jordan index to 3-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank lifts Jordan index to 3-yr high.

text.p: Jordan's official stock market index soared to a three-year high on Wednesday, driven up by sustained local demand for Arab Bank shares.
Brokers attribute the bank's recent popularity to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
Arab Bank stock, which has risen eight percent in the last week, gained 6.5 dinars to end weekly trade at 286 dinars ($403) after dominating market turnover throughout the week.
"Arab Bank is driving the market," said broker Husam al-Hanbali.

The bank's rise pushed the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index up 0.76 percent to 165.40 points, its highest level since March 1994. It accounted for half of Wednesday's 1.5 million dinars turnover.
"There are expectations that the scrapping of the ownership ceiling could be approved by cabinet next week," Hanbali said.

Arab Bank shares are now at a five-year high and the market's official index -- highly sensitive to moves in the price of the stock which accounts for almost one third of the Amman bourse's 3.4 billion dinar capitalisation -- has matched their gains.
Other indices, less heavily weighted in favour of the bank, paint a less rosy picture of the market's health.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, is languishing down at 80.71 points, up just 0.19 percent on the day and still 3.22 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
